fields.meta_title: Home Valuation Landing Page Builder for Agents | Emergent
fields.meta_description: A home valuation landing page turns an address into a seller lead. See four agent examples and build one that alerts you to each owner.
fields.h1: Build a Home Valuation Landing Page That Finds Sellers
fields.hero_description: Build a home valuation landing page that asks for the address first and saves every owner's request to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Home Valuation Page Needs
fields.features_subheading: An owner trades an address for a price range. Six parts handle that trade, and Emergent changes any of them by prompt.
fields.feature_1:
The address comes first, the email second

Emergent builds the form in two steps. Step one asks only for the street address. Step two asks for a name, email, and phone, once the owner has typed the house they care about.
fields.feature_2:
Questions that shape the price range

Ask for beds, baths, square footage, and the year of the last kitchen update. Each answer is saved as its own column, so you can prepare the range with the details in front of you.
fields.feature_3:
A plain label under every number

Write one line, such as "An estimate, not an appraisal", and the page shows it under each price range it displays. Change the wording later with a single message to Emergent.
fields.feature_4:
An alert for every owner who asks

The app sends you an email or a Slack message with the address and the owner's selling timeline as each new request lands. Point the alert at one agent or at a team channel.
fields.feature_5:
Valuation data and your CRM, by API

Connect a valuation data service you license, or your CRM, over its API. The page can show that service's range, and each request syncs to the CRM as a new contact with the address.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain or your own copy of the code

Host the page on Emergent under a custom domain (custom domains use credits), or export the page and its request table to your GitHub repository on paid plans and run it yourself.

fields.tab_content_1:
A written range by the next business day, then a walkthrough

Delphine Arroway works alone, so her page puts the address on step one and the contact details on step two. The app emails her each request with the bed and bath count. She replies with a written price range by the next business day. In October, 41 owners asked, and 7 of them booked a walkthrough.
fields.tab_content_2:
The range shows after the owner types an email

Coralind Realty connects a valuation data service it licenses to the page over that service's API. An owner at 18 Birchlow Lane enters the address and an email, and the page shows a low of $388,000 and a high of $421,000. Under the numbers: "An estimate, not an appraisal." The request is saved with that range.
fields.tab_content_3:
Sellers within 3 months, all sent to Radomir in Slack

Tollesby Home Team asks one timing question: when might you sell? A pick of within 3 months posts to the #listings Slack channel with Radomir Pardoe tagged. Every other request gets a follow-up reminder 90 days out. Of 58 requests in October, 12 picked within 3 months.
fields.tab_content_4:
23 Sunnimeade owners asked after one postcard run

Cyrus Nowell mailed 600 postcards to Sunnimeade, each with a QR code that opens his page. The page lists the last 3 sales he enters by hand, above a short request form. Each request saves the street. Within 30 days, 23 owners asked for a range, and 6 of them live on Hollins Vale Court.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Home Valuation Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a home valuation landing page that owners finish and agents can answer, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the address on screen one
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Label every number as an estimate
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose whether you write each price range yourself or pull one from a data provider over its API. That choice sets what the page promises: a reply from you later, or a number on screen as soon as the owner gives an email.
fields.howto_step_2_des: An owner who has typed in the house is already invested in the answer. Keep the first screen to that single field, wide enough for a unit number, and hold the contact fields for screen two.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask only what changes the range, such as the room count and when the kitchen was last redone. Leave the mortgage balance and the reason for selling to the first phone call, where you can ask in context.
fields.howto_step_4_des: The CFPB describes an appraisal as an independent assessment of the value of the property. A range on a lead page is not one. Say that in plain words under every number the page shows, and repeat it in the email you send back.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Route owners by when they might sell
fields.howto_step_5_des: Ask one timing question with fixed answers, such as within 3 months, in 6 months, in a year, or not sure. Send the near-term answers to the agent who takes listings, and set a follow-up date for everyone else.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write the steps, the questions, the label, and who hears about each request in one message. Emergent builds the page, the form, and the request table, and each later change, like a new question, is one more prompt.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Send a test request from your phone
fields.howto_step_7_des: Scan your own QR code or tap your own ad, then submit a request for a real address. Confirm the alert reaches the right person, and that the row in the table carries the street and the timeline you picked.

faq_plan.q: What is a home valuation landing page?
faq_plan.a: A home valuation landing page is a single page where a homeowner enters an address and asks what the house might sell for. The agent behind it gets a seller lead with the property details attached, and the owner gets a price range back, on screen or by email.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a home valuation landing page?
faq_plan.a: Tell Emergent's AI landing page builder what the page needs in one message: the address step, the questions after it, the line that labels the estimate, and who gets each request. Emergent builds the page with a table behind it for every request, and you change any part by sending another message.

faq_plan.q: What should a home value landing page ask for?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the street address first, then a name and an email or phone number. Add only the details you need to price the house, such as bed and bath counts. Cut any field you would not use when you prepare the range.

faq_plan.q: Is the estimate on a home valuation landing page an appraisal?
faq_plan.a: No. According to the CFPB, an appraisal is a written document that shows an opinion of how much a property is worth. The range on a lead page comes from the agent or from a data provider the agent connects. Label it as an estimate wherever it appears.

faq_plan.q: Should a home valuation landing page show the price before the email?
faq_plan.a: Either works, and each changes what you get back. Showing the range after an email is entered gives you a contact for every number you hand out. Promising a written range later gives you time to study the house first, and a reason to call.

faq_plan.q: How do I show an automatic price range on a home valuation landing page?
faq_plan.a: Connect a valuation data provider you license over its API, and the page can show that provider's range after the owner submits. A page built on Emergent connects to any tool with an API. Without a provider, the page saves the request and you write the range yourself.

faq_plan.q: Where do requests from a home valuation landing page go after an owner submits?
faq_plan.a: Each request lands as a row with the address and every answer the owner gave. On Emergent, that table sits in a database you own. The app can also email you or post to a Slack channel as each request arrives.

faq_plan.q: How do I follow up on home valuation landing page leads who sell later?
faq_plan.a: Ask when the owner might sell, and give each answer its own next step. A near-term seller goes to an agent the same day. A later seller gets a reminder on your calendar, such as 90 days out, to check in with fresh sales nearby.

faq_plan.q: Can I make a home valuation landing page for one neighborhood postcard mailing?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Point the postcard QR code at a page built for that one neighborhood, list the recent sales you want owners to see, and save the street with each request. A count by street then shows which part of the neighborhood answered.

faq_plan.q: Can a home valuation landing page use my brokerage's domain name?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. On a paid plan, you can instead export the code to your GitHub repository and host the page yourself.

plan.angle: The top 10 for home valuation landing page is real estate landing page roundups and home value estimator lists: they show that agents put a 'what is my home worth' page first, never what happens to the request after the owner types an address. This page shows four agent setups (a solo agent who prepares each range by hand, a brokerage that shows a range from a valuation service it licenses, a team that routes owners by selling timeline, and a neighborhood postcard page), each with the form, the alert or rule behind it and the row it lands in, and it says plainly that an online estimate is a lead tool, not an appraisal.
